text: Two nursing-home admission agreements required arbitration for every dispute but one exception: claims to collect late payments owed by the patient.
provenance: No carve-out for late payments. Nothing about who pays to file.

text: The paper therefore sent negligence and death claims to a private arbitrator while preserving a courthouse path for collecting an unpaid bill.
provenance: A dispute about how somebody died goes to a private arbitrator. A dispute about an unpaid bill stays in a courthouse.

text: A family member had signed each agreement on behalf of a patient who required extensive nursing care.
provenance: In each case, a family member of a patient requiring extensive nursing care had signed an agreement with a nursing home on behalf of the patient.

text: The Supreme Court's short opinion provides no ages, conditions, admission dates, death dates, or details of the alleged care.
provenance: No ages. No conditions. No dates of admission, no dates of death.

text: The same two contracts also placed the arbitration filing fee on whichever party filed first, without stating a dollar figure.
provenance: Whoever starts the proceeding pays to start it. The opinion states no dollar figure.
